bookTitle: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets

facts.statement: The daily bar chart plots price on the vertical axis and time on a 5-day horizontal axis. Each vertical bar spans the session high and low, with a left horizontal tic marking the opening price and a right horizontal tic marking the critical closing price.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Chart Construction: Chart Types, Scales, Volume & Open Interest
sourceCitation.excerpt: A single vertical bar represents the entire price range between the period's high and low; Open Price is marked by a left tic and Close Price by a right tic [1, 3].

facts.statement: On a bar chart, the closing price represents the most critical valuation of the trading session. Price gaps, which are spaces where no trading occurs between bars, act as direct markers of market urgency: upside gaps signal strength while downside gaps signal weakness.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Chart Construction: Chart Types, Scales, Volume & Open Interest
sourceCitation.excerpt: The closing price is considered the most critical price of the trading day [5]. Price gaps act as markers of urgency [6].

facts.statement: A line chart (close-only chart) connects successive closing prices with a continuous line. Proponents argue that intraday highs and lows represent temporary market noise, making the settlement or closing price the purest and most valid measure of true market value.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Chart Construction: Chart Types, Scales, Volume & Open Interest
sourceCitation.excerpt: Many technicians consider intraday highs and lows to be temporary noise and regard the closing price as the most valid measure of true market value [5, 7, 8].

facts.statement: Point and Figure (P&F) charts measure pure price movement by plotting rising prices as columns of X's and falling prices as columns of O's while ignoring time and volume on the horizontal axis. If price fails to meet the box threshold, the chart remains unchanged.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Chart Construction: Chart Types, Scales, Volume & Open Interest
sourceCitation.excerpt: A Point & Figure chart measures pure price movement while ignoring time and volume as separate entities on the x-axis [9, 10, 11].

facts.statement: Point and Figure sensitivity is governed by box size and reversal criteria: 1-box reversals capture intraday and short-term action, 3-box reversals (standard Chartcraft method) filter for intermediate-term trends, and 5-box reversals provide high compression for long-term trend analysis.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Chart Construction: Chart Types, Scales, Volume & Open Interest
sourceCitation.excerpt: 1-Box Reversal: intraday/short-term; 3-Box Reversal: standard intermediate-term (Chartcraft); 5-Box Reversal: highly compressed long-term analysis [12, 15-17].

facts.statement: The 3-box reversal Point and Figure horizontal count projects upside or downside price objectives by multiplying the number of columns across a congestion base or top by the reversal value (box size multiplied by the reversal criterion), then adding or subtracting from the base.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Chart Construction: Chart Types, Scales, Volume & Open Interest
sourceCitation.excerpt: Reversal Value = Box Size * Reversal Criteria; Target Objective = Pattern Base/Top Price +/- (Number of Columns * Reversal Value) [13, 20].

variables.definition: Pattern base price (for upside target) or top price (for downside target)
Number of columns across the congestion area
Reversal criteria threshold (e.g., 3 for a 3-box reversal chart)

facts.statement: On a 3-box reversal Point and Figure chart with a $1.00 box size, the reversal value equals $3.00 ($1.00 multiplied by 3). If a congestion base spans 10 columns across, multiplying 10 columns by the $3.00 reversal value yields a $30.00 projected move above the base.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Chart Construction: Chart Types, Scales, Volume & Open Interest
sourceCitation.excerpt: A 10-column base on a $1.00 box, 3-box reversal chart yields a $3.00 reversal value (1 x 3) and a target projection of $30.00 (10 x 3) above the base [13, 20].

facts.statement: To apply moving averages to timeless Point and Figure charts, the technician first computes the average price of each individual column by summing the prices of all X's or O's in that column and dividing by the count of boxes, then smooths across 10 or 20 columns.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Chart Construction: Chart Types, Scales, Volume & Open Interest
sourceCitation.excerpt: Column Average Price = Sum of Prices of X's or O's in Column / Number of X's or O's in Column, smoothed over 10 or 20 columns [21].

variables.definition: Average price of the specific X or O column
Price value of the i-th X or O box within the column
Total number of X's or O's in the column

facts.statement: A basic Point and Figure buy signal occurs when an X column rises one box above the prior X column peak, while a sell signal triggers when an O column falls one box below the prior O column low. A breakout from a post-move congestion 'fulcrum' is termed a catapult.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Chart Construction: Chart Types, Scales, Volume & Open Interest
sourceCitation.excerpt: Buy Signal: X column rises one box above prior X peak; Sell Signal: O column falls one box below prior O low; breakout from fulcrum is a catapult [11, 22-24].

facts.statement: Unlike bar chart trendlines that connect multiple swing points, 3-box reversal Point and Figure trendlines are drawn strictly at 45-degree angles. Bullish support lines slant 45 degrees upward from beneath the lowest O box, while bearish resistance lines slant 45 degrees downward from above the highest X box.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Chart Construction: Chart Types, Scales, Volume & Open Interest
sourceCitation.excerpt: 3-Box Reversal Trendlines are drawn strictly at 45-degree angles starting under the lowest O box of a bottom or above the highest X box of a top [25].

facts.statement: Kenneth Tower's logarithmic Point and Figure method assigns percentage box sizes to capture multi-year trends: using a 3.6% box on AOL projected targets of 69.7 and 136.5, a 3.2% box on Intel projected 33 and 87.6, and 10/20-column averages on a 2.7% Royal Dutch chart maintained a 1993-1997 long position.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Chart Construction: Chart Types, Scales, Volume & Open Interest
sourceCitation.excerpt: Intel Corp (3.2% box), America Online (3.6% box), and Royal Dutch Petroleum (2.7% logarithmic P&F with 10/20-column moving averages, 1993-1997) [14, 26-29].

facts.statement: Japanese candlesticks display the range between the open and close as a rectangular 'real body'—colored white (open) when the close exceeds the open, and black when the close falls below the open. Thin vertical lines above and below the body, called shadows or wicks, mark session extremes.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Chart Construction: Chart Types, Scales, Volume & Open Interest
sourceCitation.excerpt: Real Body: rectangular section between Open and Close (white if Close > Open, black if Close < Open); Shadows represent session high and low [30, 33].

facts.statement: Spinning tops feature small real bodies with long upper and lower shadows, signaling market indecision. A Doji forms when open and close prices are virtually identical, with key variants including the Long-legged Doji (extreme indecision), bearish Gravestone Doji (long upper shadow only), and bullish Dragonfly Doji (long lower shadow only).

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Chart Construction: Chart Types, Scales, Volume & Open Interest
sourceCitation.excerpt: Spinning Tops indicate indecision; Doji forms when Open and Close are equal, including Long-legged, Gravestone, and Dragonfly variants [34-36].

facts.statement: Two-day candlestick reversals require a 50% body penetration threshold: in a bearish Dark Cloud Cover, Day 2 opens above Day 1's long white candle high but closes well below its real body midpoint; in a bullish Piercing Line, Day 2 opens lower than Day 1's black candle but closes above its midpoint.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Chart Construction: Chart Types, Scales, Volume & Open Interest
sourceCitation.excerpt: Dark Cloud Cover closes well below the midpoint of Day 1's white body; Piercing Line opens lower but closes above the midpoint of Day 1's black body [37].

facts.statement: Morning Star (bullish) and Evening Star (bearish) are three-candle reversal patterns comprising a long body, a small gapping star body, and a strong counter-trend third candle. Conversely, the Rising Three Methods is a five-candle bullish continuation pattern where three small counter-trend bodies remain inside Day 1's long white range.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Chart Construction: Chart Types, Scales, Volume & Open Interest
sourceCitation.excerpt: Morning/Evening Star: three-candle turning patterns; Rising Three Methods: five-candle bullish continuation with three small bodies inside Day 1's range [38-40].

generalAssumptions: Market action discounts all known and unknown fundamentals.
Prices move in trends, and a trend in motion is more likely to continue than to reverse.
The closing price represents the most critical consensus valuation of the trading session, filtering out temporary intraday noise.
